classification.difficultyReason: Read the centre and radius, then find intercepts by setting x=0 and y=0. Part a gives surd intercepts and part b a tangency. Same as p11-q3 parts d to h.

content.prompt:
Sketch the following circles.
Label the coordinates of the centre and intercepts, if any.

questionDiagrams.code:
% mathsmap-diagram-colours {"version":1,"kind":"graph","base":[],"semantic":[],"reference":"slot-5-q-a-axes"}
\begin{tikzpicture}\special{dvisvgm:raw <metadata data-graph-strokes="1"/>}\draw[<->,line width=.5pt](-2,0)--(2,0) node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->,line width=.5pt](0,-2)--(0,2) node[above]{$y$};\end{tikzpicture}

answer.worked:
Centre $(3,-2)$, radius $4$.
Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x-3)^2+(0+2)^2&=16\\(x-3)^2&=12\\x&=3\pm2\sqrt3\end{aligned}$$
Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}(0-3)^2+(y+2)^2&=16\\(y+2)^2&=7\\y&=-2\pm\sqrt7\end{aligned}$$
Sketch the circle with these intercepts and centre.

answer.worked:
Centre $(5,4)$, radius $4$.
Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x-5)^2+(0-4)^2&=16\\(x-5)^2&=0\\x&=5\end{aligned}$$
Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}(0-5)^2+(y-4)^2&=16\\(y-4)^2&=-9\end{aligned}$$
There are no real $y$-intercepts. Sketch the circle tangent to the $x$-axis at $(5,0)$.
